### Observed differences

- Five activities — A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 — disappeared from the traces. In the earlier window each ran in a minority of cases (A21 in about 25 of 100 traces, A14 about 22, A22 about 20, A15 about 18, A20 about 17), always exactly once per trace; in the later window none of the five appears in any of the 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- In the earlier window these five behaved as mutually exclusive alternatives: no trace contained two of them together, and in roughly 54–66 of 100 traces none of them ran. In the later window every trace contains none of them. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012]
- In the earlier window, A38's observed outgoing transitions were split entirely across these five activities (about 25% to A21, 22% to A14, 20% to A22, 18% to A15, 17% to A20); in the later window A38 leads only to A23. [DIR006]
- In the earlier window, each of the five activities was always followed by A23 (its only observed outgoing edge), and A38 always preceded it; in the later window A23 occurs alone in every trace. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL005, REL006, REL013, REL014]
- The distance from A38 to A23 shortened from two event positions (one activity in between) in all 200 earlier traces to one position (immediate succession) in all 200 later traces. [LAG001]
- A23 itself ran in every trace in both windows, at a slightly earlier mean relative position afterwards (about 0.40 vs 0.38 of the trace). [POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the block of five alternative activities (A14, A15, A20, A21, A22) that previously sat between A38 and A23 is no longer executed: in the earlier window A38 passed each case on to exactly one of the five alternatives, which in turn always led to A23, whereas in the later window A38 leads directly to A23 and none of the five is observed. [DIR006, LAG001, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL005, REL006, REL013, REL014]

The hypothesis rests on direct and mutually consistent signs: the successor profile of A38 moved completely from the five activities to A23, the A38-to-A23 distance fell from two positions to one in every trace, the five activities fell from about 17–25 in 100 traces to zero observed occurrences, and their pairwise relations confirm they were alternatives executed between A38 and A23. The volume of flagged items (32, against roughly 0.42 expected for an unchanged process) cannot be explained by random re-sampling of the two windows. [DIR006, LAG001, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL005, REL006, REL013, REL014]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the five activities still execute at a rate too low to appear in 200 traces rather than having been removed entirely; zero participation only means they were not observed. Within the observed traces, however, A38 never routes to them any more. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006]

Other differences: none beyond the slight advance of A23's mean position, which is consistent with the same change. [POS006]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 85 units tested, 32 items qualified, 0.42 expected without change. That's a count many times larger than the expectation (32 vs 0.42, roughly 76x). So the screening comparison says the number of items cannot be explained by chance. This is control_flow family only (no time or resource items present — no TWAIT, no ASSIGN/CONC/HAND). So I should not discuss time or resources.

Evidence items:

OCC001–OCC005: activities A14, A15, A20, A21, A22 each had participation ~0.165–0.245 in the before window (i.e., about 16–25 in 100 traces) and 0.0 in the after window (0 traces). Support before: 33–49 traces; after: 0. So these five activities disappeared entirely from the after window.

DIR001–DIR005: for each of A14, A15, A20, A21, A22, the outgoing transitions before were entirely to A23 (share 1.0), and after the profile is empty (activity not observed). So each of these activities, when it occurred, was always followed by A23.

DIR006: A38's outgoing transitions: before, A38 led to A20 (0.165), A14 (0.215), A21 (0.245), A15 (0.18), A22 (0.195) — these shares sum to 1.0 (0.165+0.215+0.245+0.18+0.195 = 1.0). After, A38 leads only to A23 (1.0). So A38 previously branched to one of the five activities (each followed by A23), and now goes directly to A23. This is a bypass: the five activities formed a block between A38 and A23, and now A38 goes directly to A23.

POS001–POS005: positions of the five activities around 0.35–0.38 of the trace (relative position), support 0 after. Consistent with disappearance.

POS006: A23's position: before mean ~0.397, after ~0.378 — slightly earlier position, support 200 in both. Small shift (observed_change 0.0197). Consistent with the block being removed: A23 now occurs slightly earlier in traces.

REL001–REL004, REL007–REL012: pairs among the five activities: before, they never co-occurred (cooccurrence 0.0), each appeared alone in some traces, "neither" in ~54–66% of traces; after, "neither" = 1.0. So the five activities were mutually exclusive alternatives (only one per trace, never together), and now none of them occur.

REL005: A14 & A23: before, cooccurrence 0.215 (A14 always with A23, A14 before A23 in 0.215), B_only (A23 only) 0.785; after, B_only 1.0. So A14 always preceded A23 when it occurred; now A23 occurs alone.

REL006: A14 & A38: before, cooccurrence 0.215, B_before_A 0.215 (A38 before A14); after, B_only 1.0. So A38 preceded A14.

REL013: A21 & A23: before cooccurrence 0.245, A_before_B 0.245 (A21 before A23); after B_only 1.0.

REL014: A21 & A38: before cooccurrence 0.245, B_before_A 0.245 (A38 before A21); after B_only 1.0.

LAG001: A38 → A23 lag: before, the gap was 2 steps (component "2": 1.0); after, gap is 1 step ("1": 1.0). So A38 was followed two positions later by A23 (with one of the five activities in between), and now A23 immediately follows A38. This directly shows the bypass: the intermediate activity was removed.

So the picture: In the before window, A38 was followed (within five steps) by one of five mutually exclusive alternative activities {A14, A15, A20, A21, A22}, each of which was always followed by A23. In the after window, none of the five activities occur, and A38 leads directly to A23, with the A38→A23 gap shrinking from 2 steps to 1 step. A23 occurs in all traces in both windows (support 200/200), slightly earlier in position.

This is a classic "bypass" pattern: a block of alternative activities between A38 and A23 was removed/skipped. The hypothesis: a group of activities (A14, A15, A20, A21, A22) that previously executed as alternatives between A38 and A23 is no longer executed; A38 now connects directly to A23.

Support level: The screening shows 32 items vs 0.42 expected — many times larger, so chance can't explain the whole set. The hypothesis is directly supported by relational/directional evidence: DIR006 shows A38's transitions redistributed from the five activities to A23 alone; LAG001 shows the A38→A23 distance shrinking from 2 to 1; REL items show the five activities never co-occurring (alternatives) and disappearing; OCC items show zero participation after. This is direct, consistent evidence. I'd say "Supported hypothesis".

Wait — need to check the condition about "change in how often existing paths are taken": this is not that case, because the activities are (nearly) absent in the after window — zero participation. So it's a removal/bypass, not a path-frequency shift. The instructions say: "It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window, when a predecessor now leads directly to a successor so that a group of activities is bypassed". So this is a bypass — activities removed/skipped. That's fine; the hypothesis is that the block is bypassed/removed.

Is it "Supported hypothesis" or "Weak hypothesis"? The evidence is direct and consistent: DIR006 (A38 now leads only to A23), LAG001 (gap 2→1), OCC (five activities at zero participation), REL (co-occurrence with A23/A38 gone). All items agree. The competing explanation: could the five activities have moved elsewhere in the process rather than being removed? POS shows their support is 0 after — they were not observed anywhere in the after window. Zero participation only means not observed. With 200 traces and before-participation of 16–25%, observing 0 in 200 traces after is strong evidence they stopped occurring (or occur at a drastically lower rate). The evidence cannot rule out that they occur at a very low rate below detection, or that they moved to a position... no, participation is whole-trace, so if they occurred anywhere they'd be counted. So the alternative is they became much rarer rather than fully absent. That's a minor caveat.

Another competing explanation: sampling — a rare variant appearing in one window only. But five activities each at 16–25% participation all dropping to 0 simultaneously, plus DIR006 and LAG001 changes, is not explainable by chance (screening confirms: 32 items vs 0.42 expected).

So: Supported hypothesis. The hypothesis: the segment of five alternative activities (A14, A15, A20, A21, A22) between A38 and A23 is no longer executed; A38 now leads directly to A23. In the earlier window, each trace that passed through this block took exactly one of the five alternatives (they never co-occurred), A38 always preceded the chosen activity, and the chosen activity was always followed by A23 (gap of 2 between A38 and A23). In the later window, none of the five occur, A38's outgoing transitions go entirely to A23, and the A38→A23 gap is 1 step. A23 itself still occurs in every trace, slightly earlier (mean relative position ~0.40 → ~0.38).

Other differences: POS006 shows A23's position shifted slightly earlier — this is part of the main hypothesis consequence, actually. I could mention it as consistent with the bypass rather than a separate difference. The instruction: "If the evidence also shows other differences that are not part of this hypothesis, report them afterwards under 'Other differences:'". The A23 position shift is a consequence of the main hypothesis, so I can fold it into the main description. There are no other differences. So maybe no "Other differences" section needed, or state none.

- Use rounded percentages or fractions: e.g., "about 22 in 100 traces" for 0.215; A21 0.245 ≈ 25 in 100; A15 0.18 ≈ 18 in 100; A20 0.165 ≈ 17 in 100; A22 0.195 ≈ 20 in 100.
- Compare both windows for each difference.
